title: The Company at Ash Camp
player_facing_question: Who lived at the abandoned camp, how close did they come to release, and what private change reached the Record before it could have learned it honestly?
plausible_initial_belief: The camp belonged to anonymous failed players who missed a final answer or abandoned the server when the puzzles became too difficult.
human_stake: mkept, Ash, Rook, and Wren were friends and coworkers with jokes, resentments, ordinary jobs, and an almost-finished plan. Reconstructing them makes the later betrayal personal instead of a lore twist.
earned_belief: Four real modern investigators reached the release threshold with the needed knowledge and components. Their run failed through interference after a private route revision leaked, not through ignorance.
required_inference: Players infer four lives from overlapping work traces that another person can authenticate, reconstruct an archive route from provenance, and prove the team possessed a viable release plan. Merely naming four jobs, naming the four people, or entering ASH-13 is insufficient.
callback: Copperline service 1842 and ticket 9137 return as ordinary infrastructure the prior company used. A camera joke, Rook's correction habit, and Wren's distance estimate become evidence only after the camp is understood.

consequence.minecraft: Four workstations receive owner cards written as biographies rather than solve labels; Locker 13 opens once and issues the Witness Spool.
consequence.copperline: The owner-recovery set restores an ordinary camp thread, then preserves the private revision window without rewriting older posts.
consequence.discord: The docket records readiness, the private object and version window, and leaves the sender uncommitted for P10.

spaces.job: shared sleeping, cooking, planning, and argument space
spaces.composition: four non-identical bedrolls, repaired stove, central plan table, damp clothes line, mug shelf, discarded card game, one empty chair kept in the circle
spaces.navigation: open central gathering area with four workstation spokes
spaces.affordance: personal objects and occupied surfaces establish owners before any investigative use

spaces.job: admin, camera, building, and companion work
spaces.composition: mkept console and ticket box, Ash camera bench and numbered lockers, Rook material mock-up and counter-marks, Wren narrow writing table and route copies
spaces.navigation: wide linear row with distinct silhouettes and visible contents
spaces.affordance: four visibly different workstation grammars prevent generic right-click scanning

spaces.job: compare map/notebook/media custody and release readiness
spaces.composition: torn map table, notebook lightbox, supply tags, readiness board, Locker 13, spool reader

evidence.title: Supper ledger
evidence.author: mkept, Ash, Rook, Wren
evidence.provenance: camp stove drawer; four recurring hands match work notes
evidence.content: mkept: beans again. Ash: call them archival beans. Rook: the north shelf is not a shelf until somebody stops sitting on it. Wren: I moved. Rook: you moved the note. On the last line Ash adds: buy four cups that do not all look like mkept's cup.
evidence.accessibility: transcription identifies handwriting without requiring visual comparison
evidence.clue_job: Establishes four distinct people and relationships without acting as a lock.

evidence.title: mkept's maintenance trail
evidence.author: mkept
evidence.medium: server console notebook and Copperline ticket drafts
evidence.provenance: ticket language matches account posts; timestamps align with camp offline windows
evidence.content: mkept documented restarts, corrupt chunks, and attachment mirrors in practical language. A draft says: If I vanish from the account, keep the checksums. A person can lose a login without becoming imaginary.
evidence.clue_job: Connects the real C01 account owner to the camp administrator.

evidence.title: Ash's camera log
evidence.author: Ash
evidence.medium: shot list, batteries, and locker jokes
evidence.provenance: shot numbers match fixed clip slates; locker 13 appears as ordinary storage before becoming a key
evidence.content: 06 base check: Rook swears wall moved. 07 Wren says I am filming the wrong doorway. 08 film Wren saying it again for scientific value. Locker 13: do not let mkept store cables in here. This means you, mkept.
evidence.accessibility: shot list transcription and described props
evidence.clue_job: Makes ASH-13 a grounded owner-plus-locker relationship rather than a floating code.

evidence.title: Rook's corrections
evidence.author: Rook
evidence.medium: full-scale brace mock-up and blunt margin notes
evidence.provenance: three-notch counter-mark repeats on later Protocol Bridge; fresh blocked-route change dated after group plan
evidence.content: Do not give the Record the route you intend to walk. Build one brace, publish another, keep the counter-mark private. Margin to Wren: stop calling structural changes moods. The wall does not have a mood. It has load.
evidence.accessibility: counter-mark has text/shape diagram; no exact block alignment required
evidence.clue_job: Establishes Rook's private revision and an independent verification habit.

evidence.title: Wren's distance copies
evidence.author: Wren
evidence.provenance: sent to different companions; two distances conflict with supply and map records
evidence.content: Wren's earliest copy accurately places the camp. After the private bridge revision he lengthens the north walk in messages to Ash and shortens it in the shared plan. A final note says: I needed there to be more distance between us and the room. There wasn't.
evidence.clue_job: Locates camp by contradiction and plants fear without yet proving betrayal.

evidence.title: Earned Copperline route
evidence.author: Rook and mkept
evidence.medium: supply provenance, notebook columns, and torn-map overlay
evidence.provenance: ROOK column key comes from signed supply lots; map notch matches camp drain; service/ticket values were earned in P1
evidence.content: ACCOUNT / COMMUNITY / POST / TICKET / ARCHIVE resolves through service 1842, ticket 9137, and locker 13. The operation is recoverable from both notebook provenance and the supplied overlay; container ordering is not a solve prerequisite.
evidence.accessibility: pre-aligned overlay alternative retains inference but removes motor/vision dependence
evidence.clue_job: Creates a fair return to the lived-in Copperline archive.

evidence.title: Ash clip and contact sheet
evidence.author: Ash
evidence.medium: hash-bound clip 1 and two fixed stills
evidence.provenance: clip_01_ash_locker exact SHA-1 844c2aaf8fb51836add4b59e81abe4131c8d6d0a; revealed only after archive route finding
evidence.content: The camera-station leaf mark and grouped latch cuts five/five/three resolve ASH-13 when compared with Ash's already-established workstation. The same still shows the bridge mock-up before Rook's private revision.
evidence.accessibility: captioned transcript, high-contrast stills, and described latch grouping
evidence.clue_job: Opens the correct locker while preserving a second, later-important visual fact.

evidence.title: Near-release board and Witness Spool
evidence.author: all four; spool channel unknown
evidence.medium: completed readiness board and protected packet spool
evidence.provenance: component checks predate failure; spool contains the private revision after Rook changed it but before any public copy
evidence.content: The board marks cistern proof, system repairs, six affidavits, bridge plan, and empty seventh slot as understood. The spool reproduces Rook's private north-brace change with the team's names attached. Their missing item was not an answer; someone transmitted the plan.
evidence.accessibility: packet index and readiness text duplicate waveform/visual forms
evidence.clue_job: Ends P9 on a leak question rather than prematurely naming Wren.

conclusions.prompt: Who lived at the camp, and which shared trace lets another person authenticate each life?
required_concepts: Rook marks shared brace and repairs camp use
Wren walks route with Ash and retains copies
accepted_answers: mkept kept Ash's frames and Rook's notebook mirror stable; Ash photographed Rook's repaired brace; Rook privately marked the shared brace and kept repairing what the others used; Wren walked the changed route with Ash and retained both distance copies.

conclusions.prompt: Why did their release attempt fail?
accepted_answers: The four had the needed conclusions and components; their attempt failed after Rook's private bridge revision and their identities reached the Record, so interference—not a missing answer—stopped them.

conclusions.prompt: What question does Locker 13 carry forward?
accepted_answers: The Witness Spool contains Rook's private revision before it was public, proving a leak from inside the four-person company; P9 does not yet prove which person sent it.

meaningful_wrong_theories.theory: They were disposable player avatars represented by four stations.
meaningful_wrong_theories.response: The board returns owner labels and asks for relationships: shared meals, arguments, jokes, apologies, and cross-authored work are independent evidence of four people.

meaningful_wrong_theories.theory: They failed because the release instruction was incomplete.
meaningful_wrong_theories.response: The readiness board records every answer class and component; the open question is how a private route and their names reached the Spool.

meaningful_wrong_theories.theory: Wren is already proven by his inconsistent distance.
meaningful_wrong_theories.response: The inconsistency establishes fear and opportunity, not transmission. The docket preserves Wren as a live theory and opens P10's attribution work.

hints.H0: Treat the camp as a home and workplace before treating it as a code surface.
hints.H1: Assign each ordinary object or note to a person, then look for work that crosses two stations.
hints.H2: The route is earned from signed supply provenance, Rook's notebook, the torn map, and old Copperline identifiers.
hints.H3: Establish mkept/admin, Ash/camera, Rook/builder, Wren/companion; follow service 1842 + ticket 9137 + locker 13; compare the readiness board with the Witness Spool's private revision.

runtime.replay: four biographies, route derivation, clip/stills, readiness board, and spool provenance
runtime.restart: locker and spool custody reload without duplication
runtime.outage: local contact sheet and route derivation remain available; hosted media outage never auto-solves or blocks the alternative evidence path

novelty_comparison: P8 is systemic reconstruction and repair; P9 slows into domestic archaeology, human inference, and earned web/media custody. Its climax is an unresolved leak, not a gate or culprit answer.
cold_theory_paths: anonymous failed players -> four friends -> betrayed company
missing final clue -> complete readiness -> sabotage
Wren odd -> Wren suspicious -> attribution still open
